open_obligations: Check that Smit et al.'s Multi-Persona matches Liang et al.'s MAD prompts.
Note agreement intensity is a prompted target, not a measured agreement rate.
Check whether Liang et al.'s disagreement levels map onto Smit et al.'s X values.
out.other_title: MAD framework: two tit-for-tat debaters and a judge that manages the debate
out.rationale: Liang et al. propose MAD with two debaters in a 'tit for tat' state and a managing judge. Smit et al. attribute Multi-Persona to Liang et al., describing it as a MAD strategy in which an affirmative agent (angel) and a negative agent (devil) each provide an answer to a judge agent who manages the process and obtains a final solution. Smit et al. add an agreement-intensity prompt ('agree with the other agents X% of the time') applied to Multi-Persona and to other MAD systems.
out.scope: proposed EXTENDS: controlling disagreement in multi-agent debate, from fixed tit-for-tat prompting to a tunable agreement intensity

text: The authors hypothesise that how much agents agree with one another during a debate may significantly affect debating performance, and test it with a new prompting strategy that modulates agreement at the outset with the prompt 'you should agree with the other agents X% of the time', calling X the agreement intensity.
title: Agreement intensity: prompting debaters to agree X% of the time
